samples.summary: New per-cell awaited loop over the whole moved merge area inside one store batch — unbounded client/document work driven by user-created merge size
samples.evidence: For each moved merge, `for (const sref of this.mergeCoveredSrefs(anchor, merge.span))` (sheet.ts:2382) does an awaited `store.get` plus `store.set`/`store.delete` per covered cell inside the open `beginBatch()`. Merge size is unbounded: `canMergeSelection` (sheet.ts:4257-4274) imposes no area cap, so a collaborator with edit rights can merge a very large range and then drag-move it, producing one enormous batched Yorkie update (`yorkie-store.ts` pushes one closure per op into `batchOps`) that every connected client must apply, plus `rebuildMergeCoverMap()` and `expandChangedSrefsWithMergeAliases` over the same area. This is at most a self/collab availability annoyance rather than an exploit: the pre-existing source-clearing loop (sheet.ts:2346-2356) and `mergeSelection` (sheet.ts:4306-4318) already iterate a comparable number of cells, so the new code adds no real amplification beyond what an editor could already do. Attacker needs write access, which the Yorkie auth webhook already requires (packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-auth.controller.ts).

samples.summary: Merge re-creation at the destination skips the frozen-pane constraint that `canMergeSelection` enforces for every other merge-creation path
samples.evidence: `await this.store.setMerge(anchor, merge.span)` at sheet.ts:2375 writes a merge at `source anchor + delta` with no check that the resulting block straddles a frozen row/column boundary. The only other merge-creation path, `mergeSelection`, is gated by `canMergeSelection` (sheet.ts:4264-4272), which explicitly rejects selections crossing `frozenRows`/`frozenCols`. Dragging a merged block across the freeze boundary therefore persists a merge state the dedicated gate is designed to prevent. Not a permission/authorization gate — no privilege is gained — so this is an invariant bypass on an existing validation rather than a security vulnerability; flagged here only because it is a guard on the operation this diff newly reaches. Correctness lens owns the impact.

samples.summary: No authorization/read-only gate exists in the model layer for moveRangeTo, but the sole caller is gated and the server enforces write access — no bypass found
samples.evidence: I traced the only production call site, `packages/sheets/src/view/worksheet.ts:4310` (inside `startCellDragMove`), reachable only via `detectCellEdge`, which returns false when `this.readOnly` is set (worksheet.ts:3082). No keyboard/command/menu path invokes `moveRangeTo`. The new merge writes go through `Store.setMerge`/`deleteMerge`; `ReadOnlyStore` implements both as no-ops (packages/sheets/src/store/readonly.ts:256-262), and server-side write authorization for the Yorkie document is enforced independently by the auth webhook (packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-auth.controller.ts, with a spec case 'lets a share viewer read but not write'). So the diff adds no unguarded write surface. Reported as an explicit absence-of-model-level-gate observation only, not a blocking issue.
searchedFor: Grep moveRangeTo across repo (only worksheet.ts:4310 call site)
